content:
❌ Rejected the contribution.
Comment: It looks like you are working on creating an original puzzle, but please do not set the contribution status to Ready while it contains someone else's work.
The puzzle needs some changes before it can be published and approved. Please switch the state to WIP first; I'll provide detailed comments a bit later. Thanks.
Thanks for the feedback! I've switched the contribution to WIP. I'll wait for your detailed comments and address the required changes before resubmitting it for review.

Hi, thanks for the feedback. This is my first time using the CodinGame contribution feature, and I'm still learning the process. I want to be transparent that I initially used code from kozuechan, but I acknowledge that I shouldn't have submitted someone else's work as my own. I've removed that initial version and am now working on my own implementation. I'll keep the contribution in WIP while I make sure the remaining files are original. Sorry for the mistake, and thank you for helping me understand the contribution guidelines.
Thank you for your transparent response. It's understandable when trying out a new feature for the first time. Best of luck with your contribution!
Thank you for understanding and for the encouragement! I'll keep working on the puzzle and make sure everything is in order before submitting it again. I really appreciate your guidance!

I've got a rough idea of what your puzzle is about. You don't need to use the SDK to create a solo, non-competitive puzzle unless you want to do one or more of the following (as far as I can tell):

(a) Include a viewer to visualise the progress of each test case.

(b) Have a more generous execution time limit than that of ordinary non-SDK puzzles.

(c) Allow multiple valid solutions and validate them using a custom referee.

(d) Include a random test case generator.

(e) Overcome the character limits of ordinary non-SDK puzzles (10,000 characters for inputs and 1,000 for outputs).

Regarding your puzzle:

(a) Are you planning to include case visualisation? It's uncommon for an SDK-based puzzle not to have a viewer that displays graphics, although this isn't mandatory. If you do want to incorporate graphics, I'm not sure how feasible that would be when the number of chambers is large.

(b) A higher time limit seems unnecessary, although I could be wrong.

(c) This doesn't seem applicable, as each test case has a unique expected solution.

(d) This doesn't seem applicable either, as the inputs for each test case are fixed.

(e) This is the only point that seems particularly relevant. However, even with the SDK, the largest tests cases crash the referee. For example, when you run the last test case, you'll see the limit (100,000) mentioned in the message that appears when the referee crashes.

I'm inclined to think that you could simply create a non-SDK version of the puzzle and scale down the test cases to fit within the character limits (though I understand that might not preserve the puzzle's intended difficulty). That said, you're also free to decide that you'd prefer to proceed with the current SDK version and try to fix it.

Please let me know what you think, so I can tailor my further suggestions accordingly.

Thanks.

Thank you for taking the time to analyse the puzzle and explain the trade-offs. I agree that a non-SDK version may be more suitable, since graphical visualisation and custom validation aren't essential for this problem.

I'd like to try converting it to a non-SDK puzzle and carefully scaling the test cases while preserving the intended algorithmic difficulty as much as possible. I'll also review the referee's handling of the largest tests before deciding on the final constraints.

I'd appreciate any further suggestions you have about suitable constraints for a non-SDK version. Thanks again for your guidance!

Thank you for your reply.

The first thing that came to my mind was the character limits for each case in the non-SDK version:

Input: 10,000 characters (including newlines)
Output: 1,000 characters (including newlines)

If you want to maximise the size of the cases that can fit within these limits, you could consider using 0 and 1 instead of NO and YES in the output, and even removing newlines. However, these changes would come at the expense of readability. If possible, I'd recommend keeping the current output format; otherwise, you could consider the alternatives mentioned above.

I'll give this some further thought and let you know if I come up with any other points worth considering.

Also, once you've finished creating the non-SDK contribution, please make sure to keep it in WIP for review before proceeding further.

Thank you for the helpful suggestions! I’ll keep the current `YES`/`NO` output format if the test cases fit within the character limits, and consider `0`/`1` or removing newlines only if necessary.

I’ll work on the non-SDK version, check that every input and output stays within the limits, and keep the contribution in WIP for review before proceeding further.

I appreciate your guidance and look forward to any other suggestions you may have!

Hi! Thanks again for your guidance. I'd like to keep working on my existing contribution, The Fractured Archive, so that I can preserve the current review discussion and feedback.

I've tried uploading the non-SDK package, but the build process still expects a `pom.xml` file. Is it possible to convert the existing contribution from an SDK-based Solo Game to a Classic Puzzle (IN/OUT), or would I need to keep the current contribution type and make the changes within it?

I'd appreciate your advice before I make any further changes. Thank you!
You cannot convert an SDK contribution to a non-SDK one. You'll need to create a new one.

Additional points to note:

* Cases should be ordered by increasing complexity.

* Each test and its corresponding validator should form a covering the same scenario with similar parameters.

* A maximum of 25 test-validator pairs is allowed.

* Please include a variety of cases, covering graphs of different sizes and densities (both dense and sparse), varying update frequencies (frequent and infrequent), and scenarios involving self-loops and cycles.

Thank you for clarifying and for the additional suggestions!

I'll keep my current contribution in WIP and create a new Classic Puzzle (IN/OUT) contribution. I'll reorganize the test cases in increasing order of complexity, ensure each test-validator pair covers the same scenario with similar parameters, and include a variety of graph sizes, densities, update frequencies, self-loops, and cycles while staying within the character limits.

I'll keep the new contribution in WIP for review before proceeding further. I really appreciate your guidance and help in improving my puzzle!
